title: Auto Loans: Days-Past-Due Thresholds and Due Day Change Limits
content:
Several Auto Loans servicing outcomes hinge on a count of days past due or on a count of due day changes. This page lists those thresholds for every product so that a loan's standing can be read against them.

## Threshold table

| Loan product | Most days past due at which an extension can be granted | Due day changes allowed in any rolling 365 days | Largest move of the due day (calendar days) | Days past due at which the loan turns delinquent | Days past due at which remaining principal is charged off |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Used Vehicle Loan | 59 | 1 | 15 | 30 | 120 |
| Certified Pre-Owned Vehicle Loan | 59 | 1 | 15 | 30 | 120 |
| Auto Refinance Loan | 59 | 1 | 15 | 30 | 120 |
| Lease Buyout Loan | 59 | 1 | 15 | 30 | 120 |
| New Vehicle Loan | 59 | 1 | 15 | 30 | 120 |
| Green Vehicle Loan | 59 | 1 | 15 | 30 | 120 |

## The ladder of days past due

Read in ascending order, the figures form a single ladder that is the same on every product:

- at 30 days past due the loan's status becomes delinquent;
- up to and including 59 days past due a payment extension can still be granted, since 59 is the most days past due the loan may show when an extension is granted;
- at 120 days past due the remaining principal is charged off.

## Due day change limits

One change of the due day is allowed in any rolling 365-day span, and a single change can move the due day by no more than 15 calendar days in either direction.

## Hypothetical readings

A hypothetical loan showing 45 days past due is delinquent, since 45 is above 30, and is still inside the 59-day limit for an extension. A hypothetical loan at 60 days past due is beyond that limit. A request to move a due day from the 3rd to the 20th asks for a 17-day move and exceeds the 15-day limit; a move from the 3rd to the 18th, which is exactly 15 days, stays within it. These loans and dates are illustrative only.
